scope: Proposition 3.3 (Scalar profiles) of the manuscript “The metric Blaschke theorem” (preprints/The-metric-Blaschke-theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 344 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c631e2d36940a81e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Define h(t) = det(H′ (t))1/m (0 < t < T), s(t) = det(S(t))1/k (t ∈ I), si(t) = s(t + iD) (0 < t < D, i = 0, 1). (3.12) The function h is smooth and positive across D. There are positive constants cH, CH, ci, Ci, depending on the fixed geodesic and its chart, such that cH ≤ h(t) sin2 t ≤ CH (0 < t < T), (3.13) ci ≤ si(t) sin2(2t) 4 ≤ Ci (0 < t < D, i = 0, 1). (3.14) Equivalently, the logarithms of the ratios of h to 1/ sin2 t and of si to 4/ sin2(2t) are bounded.
